chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is its Measure.
chapter_note: This chapter is a hagiographic-historical riverbank scene used to introduce a dense cosmological teaching about the elemental garment of Water. The core substrate concentrates in ¶6–10 (with a small fragment in ¶8): a systematic account of First Man’s deployment of elemental garments against the rulers, including the sevenfold river-measure and the binding of the giants. The opening/closing (¶1–3, ¶12) are clearly editorial frame; ¶11 is a later devotional/exhortative wrap rather than impersonal system-teaching. One intra-Manichaean citation (“Great Gospel”) in ¶6 is a later compilation marker embedded inside otherwise core cosmology.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/biographical scene-setting tied to King Shapur and the title “apostle”; this is compilation frame, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Extended historical description of the Tigris flood with calendar detail (Phar-mouthi) and city terror; narrative staging rather than cosmological system-mapping.
Narrative continuation with institutional marker “leaders of his church” and the title “apostle”; this is editorial scene-setting around the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: How great is the power of the garment of the waters? How far shall [it extend]? That it should enter with the roar of its flood and fill this river Tigris in its vastness like the mighty sea! It has carried waves from river bank to bank, and run from wall to wall. The source from which all these waters burst forth, how great will it be? For they come and come each year at their appointed season!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution (“One of his disciples then spoke. He says to the apostle:”). The remaining text is a substantive cosmological question about the ‘garment of the waters’ embedded in the narrative scene.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-style cosmological inquiry (measure/extent/source of an elemental ‘garment’) embedded in later dialogue narrative; the narrative voice and speaker tags are later compilation frame.

Dialogue-transition with the title “apostle” and audience-direction (“listen to what I am about to tell you”); functions as rhetorical bridge into the teaching rather than the impersonal substrate itself.

paragraphs.core_text: [At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [...] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [...] those [...], the warriors of destruction [...] laboured and brought them forth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed intra-textual citation hook: “the way that I told] you in the Great Gospel.” This is a compilation-era reference to another Manichaean book, not part of the impersonal substrate exposition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Predominantly core cosmological mechanics (First Man, elements, garments, immeasurable rulers, ingestion/production of waters). The explicit appeal to an authoritative written source (“Great Gospel”) is a later compilation marker embedded in the paragraph.

paragraphs.core_text: There were seven (rivers), like the great river Tigris [that you] see, flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [...] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [...] of [...]; they were not emptied; rain and [...] their existent days.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic numerical structure (seven rivers) and internal cosmic physiology (mouth/stomach/descent/burning) stays within the cosmological system; no institutional or citation overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: The measure of that river was expanded seven times, as they flow [...] of the body of the [...] waters [...] now.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“The apostle speaks to that elect one:”) and removed the ensuing exhortative ‘Marvel…’ material as later devotional/application voice rather than impersonal system-description.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a compact, structural measure-teaching (“expanded seven times”) characteristic of the substrate, but embedded in later dialogue framing and expanded by exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] is how great a struggle, since it has [...] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [...] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [...]. These rulers [...] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [...]; all pass away [...]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic binding/entwinement of the giants and eschatological dissolution of the flesh-universe: still cosmos→cosmos description, not institution-pointing or NT citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, as this small stream is reckoned [...] before the vastness of these waters. For only one river from thousands of rivers of water, from the secrets that are not revealed, is the river Tigris upon the earth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed direct address/recital marker: “of which I have recounted to you.” This is dialogue-performance language, not part of the underlying cosmological comparison itself.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying teaching is a cosmological magnitude-comparison (earthly Tigris vs hidden ‘thousands of rivers’). The first-person ‘I…to you’ is a later speech-setting trace.

Devotional/exhortative wrap (“See… be amazed… Marvel… understand… how great is that god”), shifting from impersonal mechanics to audience-directed piety; not institutional rules, but still a later homiletic application layer rather than core substrate.
Closing disciples’ reverence/thanks formula (“We revere you, our master… opened our eyes…”): classic Kephalaia hagiographic frame closure.
